questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When anything makes road conditions less than perfect.
When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When anything makes road conditions less than perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the posted speed limit when roads are wet or slippery, when you cannot see well, or when any condition is not perfect. You can be ticketed for driving too fast for conditions, even if you are going the posted speed limit.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes distorted.
You calm down and can concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and can concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your ability to see clearly, changes how you judge speed and distance, reduces your ability to handle headlight glare, and often makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?
questions.correctAnswerText: Octagon
questions.explanation: Stop signs are octagonal (eight-sided). This shape is used only for stop signs. All eight-sided signs tell drivers to make a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.question: What should you do when a driver behind you wants to pass?

options.text: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a driver behind you wants to pass, slow down so there is enough space in front of your car for them to complete the pass. This helps them finish the maneuver quickly and safely.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing and you do not see or hear a train. When must you stop?

options.text: If a stop sign is posted.
If a crossing gate is down.
If the crossing lights are flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop before crossing railroad tracks if you see flashing red lights, a lowered crossing gate, a posted stop sign, or a flagger signaling you to stop. If you cannot see a train clearly or if it is too close to cross safely, stop. Never try to race a train.

questions.question: What must you do when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights?

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Pull to the right curb and stop.
Stop exactly where you are right now.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right curb and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle using flashing lights or hear a siren, pull to the right side of the road or curb immediately and stop.

questions.question: What should the driver of a small vehicle be prepared for when passing a large vehicle?

options.text: Wind gusts from the large vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles can create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles sideways. Drivers of small vehicles should be ready to steer correctly when passing or approaching large vehicles moving at high speeds.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights are used at dangerous intersections. Treat them the same as stop signs.

questions.question: When must you yield for emergency vehicles?

options.text: When you see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using a siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: What factors affect how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach
How much time passes between drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: All three of the above
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much alcohol you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your body weight. Eating before or while drinking slows alcohol absorption somewhat, but it cannot prevent intoxication if you drink too much.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, what must you do?

options.text: Keep driving at your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians go first.
questions.explanation: You can turn right or left at a green light unless a sign says you cannot. When you turn, you must let other cars and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: What should you do if another car is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, wait until the road ahead is clear and slowly reduce your speed to let the tailgater pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you and a right lane is open, move to it. If no right lane is open, wait for a clear road ahead and then slowly reduce your speed to let them pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the chance they will hit you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign says you cannot make a U-turn. Do not turn around where this sign is posted.

questions.question: What should you NOT do when changing lanes?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Check for other cars moving into your lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police about the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police about the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for cars behind you. Use your turn signal to tell other drivers what you plan to do. Look for other cars that may also be changing into your lane. Never use your cell phone while driving.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided highway with multiple lanes and you see or hear an emergency vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as fast as you can.
Slow down, move out of the way, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move out of the way, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, slow down, clear a path, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: How can you stay awake on long trips?

options.text: Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
Move your eyes side to side while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
questions.explanation: On long trips, take regular breaks to rest and stretch. Do this even if you do not feel tired.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic only moves in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic only moves in the direction shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This one-way sign shows that all traffic moves in only one direction, the way the arrow points.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
Getting ahead of bad drivers by passing them in traffic.
Following the car in front of you closely.
Quickly changing lanes and weaving through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you see dangerous situations and take action before an accident happens. It helps you avoid conflicts with reckless, careless, or unsafe drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to the one you came from.
The lane marked with an arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the one you came from.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that is closest to your current lane. Do not change lanes while you are turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic light ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic light is coming. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you must always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing the tracks.
Pay attention and follow all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before turning across train tracks. Always obey all signs and traffic signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicyclists.

questions.question: An "End school zone" sign means:

options.text: A reduced speed zone is starting.
A reduced speed zone has ended.

questions.correctAnswerText: A reduced speed zone has ended.
questions.explanation: Do not exceed the school zone speed limit during the times shown. The "End school zone" sign shows where the reduced speed zone ends.

questions.question: The best safety restraints in a crash are:

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
A lap/shoulder belt and an airbag together.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lap/shoulder belt and an airbag together.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chance of surviving a crash and more than double your chance of avoiding serious injury. Airbags work best with safety belts to protect you in a front-end crash. Always wear both your shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance between cars.
Drive in the right lane only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance between cars.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems without making a sudden stop. An emergency stop could cause the car behind you to hit your vehicle.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look both ways, and go only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns yellow as you near an intersection, you should:

options.text: Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will turn red soon. You should be ready to stop before the light turns red, if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Smoking while driving or getting ready to smoke:
questions.correctAnswerText: Is a distraction.
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is dangerous because it takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn yield on green.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers to yield to oncoming traffic when turning left at a green light. You may complete the turn when it is safe.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and give a turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: Crossbuck signs mean:
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn drivers to yield to trains at railroad crossings. Do not try to drive faster than a train to cross the tracks.
